sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Vigo's biggest recent step is a low-emission zone. On 27 July 2026 the city council approved the ordinance for four zones (Centro, Praza de Portugal, Calvario and Bouzas), with PSOE votes only; the PP and BNG opposed it. Restrictions are phased, starting with vehicles without an environmental label, then label B and label C, and fines reach €200. Residents and business owners in the zones, taxis and buses are exempt. It is due to enter into force within about two months of publication [0]. The first year brings only informative notices, with fines from the second [1].

On the street, the blue zone (zona azul) runs Monday to Friday from 9:00 to 14:00 and 16:00 to 20:00, free at weekends. In 2023 non-residents paid from €0.30 up to €1.45 for the two-hour maximum, and residents with the €98 annual card had no time limit [2]. A November 2025 guide gives €0.60 for one hour and €1.45 for two [3]. The city is also taking spaces away. Mechanical ramps on Rúa Pintor Colmeiro will permanently remove about 20 of the street's roughly 30 surface blue-zone spaces [5], and the Concello applied for EU funds in 2025 for a wider 'Vigo Vertical' plan of ramps, a bike lane and electric buses; we do not know the outcome [6]. At the old station the Concello turned an informal free parking strip into a 15-minute drop-off zone, because users had been using it to avoid parking fees and blue-zone limits [4]. For Christmas 2025 it applied its highest traffic-restriction level, sends intercity coaches to Samil and directs visitors to enter via the AP-9 [10].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
New supply is mostly planned rather than built. The Urbanismo department approved licences for a 302-space public-use car park in the Barrio do Cura development [19], and an agreement on the former ETEA site includes a planned underground car park, with works expected to start in about a year [20]. In October 2026 the Concello agreed to buy two plots at Alcabre, beside O Cocho beach, that already serve as improvised beach parking, and plans to turn them into free parking [21]. The Vialia shopping centre at the railway station announced about 1,600 spaces when it opened in 2021 [18]. Only 92 private garage spaces were available to rent in central Vigo in February 2025, at an average of €91 a month [22].

Three of the older underground car parks have a legal problem. In March 2023 the regional high court annulled the 2007 award of lot 1 of the concessions (Areal, Pintor Colmeiro and Policarpo Sanz) after an expert report found most spaces smaller than the tender required. It left the Concello to decide how to provide the service, and, as reported then, the ruling could still be appealed [15]. Elsewhere, the Zona Franca said in 2022 that it would convert the robotised A Laxe car park to a conventional one, which allowed its concession to be extended to 2040 [16], and Praza da Estrela added 12 charging points in 2023 [17]. The port expects 119 cruise calls in 2026 [12]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our Vigo data cover eleven car parks with 3,427 spaces, three of them within 500 m of Praza da Constitución (1,037 spaces) and four more within 1 km (1,019). Eloymar-Tranvías runs six (1,947 spaces) and WelGood Tranvías two, Calvario and Praza América (812). Empark's Telpark runs Praza de Portugal (183 spaces) under a concession awarded in 2017 [13][14], and the Zona Franca runs Praza da Estrela and A Laxe [16][17]. Prices are fairly uniform: most central car parks charge more than €2 for the first hour, up to €2.88 at Náutico Cíes [3], and Praza de Portugal has the lowest listed hourly price, €1.80 an hour and €19.90 a day [14].

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 46% on weekdays and 39% at weekends. The fullest are Praza de Portugal (61% on weekdays), Policarpo Sanz and Urzáiz (both 60%) and Calvario (54%). Praza de Portugal is both the cheapest and the busiest. The quietest are A Laxe (29%), Praza América (32%) and Pintor Colmeiro (34%, falling to 14% at weekends). Within 500 m of the centre the average is 44%, against 55% for the four car parks 500 m to 1 km out, so the car parks closest in are not the fullest.

Capacities in our feed disagree with other sources in two cases: Praza da Estrela has 88 spaces in the feed against 452 in a 2023 report, and A Laxe 397 against 184 in a 2022 plan. We treat their occupancy with caution. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ, and we have no multi-year history for Vigo.
